summary: Initial discovery on model selection and deployment mode. Cobalt has a multilingual customer-facing QA product requiring long context (up to ~8k tokens), tool-calling for live data lookups, and strict security (VPC/KMS). Discussed tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private; open-model options; quantization and context-length impacts on latency/cost. Agreed to run benchmarks and schedule tech deep dive.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jon (Redwood SE), Daniel (Cobalt CTO), Maya (ML Lead), Sandra (Security)

[00:00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round of intros?
[00:00:08] Daniel: Hi, Daniel Wu, CTO at Cobalt. We're re-evaluating model infra, mainly for our customer support QA product. lots of long conversations, multi-lingual.
[00:00:18] Maya: Maya Rivers, ML lead. we handle EN/ES/FR primarily and sometimes PT, and we have context up to six, eight thousand tokens in a single convo.
[00:00:30] Alex: Got it. Priya, do you wanna give a quick run through what Redwood can offer and typical model choices?
[00:00:36] Priya: Sure. Redwood has Hosted API, Dedicated reserved GPU pools, and Private deployments for VPC/on-prem. for models we support a catalog of open models — Mistral variants, LlamaX-ish families, and quantized forks — and we verify performance profiles. tradeoffs are generally: open models can be cheaper if you use quantization and batching, but you need to validate quality for your multilingual prompts.
[00:00:55] Sandra: Security is big for us. We need KMS integration, SSO, SOC2 stuff, and audit logs. Private is preferable if it helps with data residency.
[00:01:05] Jon: We have a private control plane option and customer-managed networking. KMS/HSM integration is supported in Private and Dedicated with Enterprise packages. for Hosted we do bring-your-own-key for some plans but there are limits.
[00:01:18] Daniel: timeline is important: pilot in 4–6 weeks, production by Q4. cost is also a driver — need predictable costs.
[00:01:26] Maya: also need tool-calling for live inventory / customer lookup. function-calling and structured outputs are a must.
[00:01:34] Priya: Redwood supports function/tool calling and structured responses. we also stream tokens and have KV/prefix caching to reduce cost on repeated context. for tool calls we recommend models with strong function-calling stability — we can test both open Llama-family variants and smaller instruction-tuned Mistral models.
[00:01:52] [00:02:00] Alex: Can you give an example of latency/cost tradeoff for 8k context?
[00:02:05] Priya: Rough numbers: Hosted with larger open-model base at 8k, token cost is higher and latency goes up linearly with context. Dedicated with optimized kernels + quantization can drop per-token cost 30–50% and improve p99 latency by ~20% depending on batch size. but you lose some flexibility unless you use compatible model variants.
[00:02:30] Maya: For multilingual, we saw Mistral do well in EN and FR but ES had some regressions; LlamaX variants gave more consistent ES performance in our in-house tests. curious how Redwood's verified profiles line up.
[00:02:45] Priya: We run model evals across languages and can share profiles. for ES specifically we can test tuned checkpoints or instruction-tuned forks. we also evaluate context-behavior for tool-calls — sometimes models forget prior entities across 6k+ tokens without KV strategies.
[00:03:05] Sandra: On compliance, will audit logs capture token-level requests and redaction? we need retention policies.
[00:03:12] Jon: Audit logs with per-request metadata are available for Dedicated/Private; Hosted has configurable retention and anonymization but enterprise plans allow longer retention in Dedicated. we'll send the SOC2 pack.
[00:03:25] Daniel: Who from Redwood will run the benchmarks?
[00:03:28] Alex: Priya will spearhead the benchmark configs; we'll need a sample dataset and language splits from you.
[00:03:35] Maya: we'll provide examples and the top-100 prompt set we use for regressions.
[00:03:40] [00:03:50] Priya: For the benchmark plan: we'll run Hosted baseline and a Dedicated optimized run — including quantized variants where applicable — and measure throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency and token cost. also measure function-call reliability and multilingual accuracy on your prompt set.
[00:04:05] Daniel: Any constraints on your side for tool-calling? we need synchronous calls to internal apis in some cases.
[00:04:12] Priya: We support sync and async patterns. for synchronous tool-calls we recommend using our Dedicated route with low-latency SLOs or Hosted with regional routing to minimize hops. we also have fallback policies to smaller models if the primary is degraded.
[00:04:28] Sandra: How do you handle private deployments in air-gapped environments?
[00:04:32] Jon: We offer an on-prem package; control plane can be customer-managed and offline. there are additional support and licensing terms for that.
[00:04:40] Maya: A question on context window expansion — do you offer dynamic sliding windows or offload to embeddings?
[00:04:45] Priya: We provide caching and dynamic KV strategies. for very long histories we often combine short context + retrieval via embeddings to reduce cost. for strict 8k sessions we can run full context but cost implications. we'll show tradeoffs in the benchmark.
[00:05:00] Alex: Any concerns about vendor lock or portability?
[00:05:04] Daniel: yes, we want model portability in case we self-host later.
[00:05:07] Priya: Redwood's deployment abstraction lets you pin model versions and move between Hosted and Dedicated/Private; we can provision exportable model assets where licensing permits.
[00:05:18] [00:05:30] Alex: Okay to recap next steps? we'll run the benchmarks, share security docs, and set up the technical deep dive.
[00:05:36] Daniel: Sounds good. also send pricing and any committed Dedicated discounts.
[00:05:40] Alex: will do. thanks everyone.
[00:05:44] Maya: thanks.
[00:05:46] Sandra: bye.

End of transcript.
